newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reports push Oil Search to year high.
newsitem.headline: Reports push Oil Search to year high.

text.p: Shares in oil and gas explorer and producer Oil Search Ltd rose to a year high on Wednesday following Tuesday's report of hydrocarbon shows in the Moran 3-X well in Papua New Guinea.
A company announcement on Wednesday also said the Moran-2X second sidetrack well had recorded high background gas readings and flourescence within the Toro sandstone.
Analysts said Tuesday's report was positive as it indicated the possible presence of an extra hydrocarbon bearing formation at Moran.
Oil Search said it had encountered hydrocarbon shows in the Moran-3X well in block PPL-161 between 1,658 metres and 1,710 metres, above its eventual target zone in the Digimu and Toro reservoirs.
The result was also positive because Oil Search held 35.017 percent of PPL-161, compared with 7.763 percent of PDL-2, where the Moran-2X well was drilled, a Sydney-based analyst said.
Oil Search said the significance of the two most recent shows would be evaluated by wireline logging.
Oil Search has previously said the Moran field has the potential to outstrip the nearby producing Kutubu field, which has recoverable reserves of more than the 305 million barrels of oil.
Shares in Oil Search were up 21 cents at A$3.78 at 2.40 p.m. (0440 GMT), just off a high of A$3.80.
